data.COMMANDS_HELP: Command List: - /help (or /h or /?) Displays this page - /version (or /ver or /about) Information about the version. - /whoami Information about you. - /whois [character name (or *account name)] Information about a character or an account. - /f a (or /f +) [character name (or *account name)] Adds the character or the account to your Friend list. - /f d (or /f - or /f r) [character name (or *account name)] Deletes the character or the account from your Friend list. - /ignore a (or /ignore +) [character name (or *account name)] Adds the player or the account to your Enemy list. - /ignore d (or /ignore - or /ignore r) [character name (or *account name)] Deletes the player or the account from your Enemy list. - /w (or /msg or /whisper) [character name (or *account name)] [message] Sends a private message to a player or an account. - /t [message] Sends the message to team members only. - /g [message] Sends the message to guild members only. - /p [message] Sends the message to the group members only. - /a [message] Sends the message to players of the same alignment who are in the same area. - /r [message] Sends a request to join a guild to players in the same area. - /b [message] Sends an offer to buy or sell items to players in the same area. - /m [message] Sends an offer to meet new adventurers to players in the same area. - /away Activates / Deactivates the "Away" mode in order to receive/block private messages. - /list (or /players) Lists the name of the characters that are fighting. - /kick [character name] Expels a player from a fight. You can earn honor points by participating in territorial conquests.
You lose honor points if a territory of your alignment is conquered by the enemy and you were not here to defend it!
If an allied territory is conquered by the enemy and you were in the area, you don't lose honor points.

You won't win honor points by attacking players of an enemy alignment.

You'll get disgrace points if you attack players with neutral alignement.

The more honor points you win, the higher your rank becomes. Ranks enable you to pay less for some services in your city... you'll also get bigger bonuses when you fight in a friendly area, and weaker penalties in enemy areas.
You can refuse to participate in the "Player versus Player" system, but you will lose some of your honor points and get lower bonuses.
